ordered.title: After Diagnostics - Your Options
ordered.description: Once you have the diagnostic report, you'll know exactly what's wrong. Here's how to decide what to do next.

cards.title: ✅ Repairable
cards.text: Isolated failure, no bottom-end damage, no metal in oil, repair cost reasonable (under 50% of vehicle value). Example: Single injector, sensor, or component failure.
cards.fullText: ✅ Repairable Isolated failure, no bottom-end damage, no metal in oil, repair cost reasonable (under 50% of vehicle value). Example: Single injector, sensor, or component failure. Get repair quotes

cards.title: 🔄 Replacement Needed
cards.text: Catastrophic failure, bottom-end damage, metal in oil, repair cost unreasonable (exceeds 50% of vehicle value). Example: Snapped timing chain, seized engine, bearing failure.
cards.fullText: 🔄 Replacement Needed Catastrophic failure, bottom-end damage, metal in oil, repair cost unreasonable (exceeds 50% of vehicle value). Example: Snapped timing chain, seized engine, bearing failure. Get replacement quotes

cards.title: ❓ Unclear / Further Investigation
cards.text: Intermittent fault, multiple possible causes, complex system fault. Example: Fault appears sometimes, ECU or wiring issue, several components could be causing the symptom.

blocks.question: How much does engine diagnostics cost? +
blocks.answer: Basic OBD2 scan £50-£100 , full system diagnostic £100-£200 , advanced inspection £200-£400 , specialist investigation £250-£500 . Prices vary by region and specialist.

blocks.question: What does engine diagnostics include? +
blocks.answer: OBD2 trouble code retrieval, code interpretation, live data analysis, component testing, and a written report with findings, recommendations, and cost estimates.

blocks.question: Do I need diagnostics before repairing or replacing? +
blocks.answer: Yes - diagnostics reveal what's actually wrong. Without diagnostics, you risk spending money on parts or repairs that don't fix the problem.

blocks.question: What happens after diagnostics? +
blocks.answer: If the issue is repairable, get repair quotes. If replacement is needed, get replacement quotes. If unclear, book advanced investigation. Get repair quotes → Get replacement quotes →

blocks.question: Can I do diagnostics myself? +
blocks.answer: You can buy an OBD2 reader and scan your own codes. However, interpreting the codes correctly requires expertise. A professional diagnostic includes live data, component testing, and a written report.

blocks.question: What if the diagnostic says my engine needs replacing? +
blocks.answer: If the diagnostic confirms catastrophic failure, get replacement quotes - used, reconditioned, rebuilt. Replacement is usually the best option for snapped chains, bearing failures, or seized engines.

blocks.question: What if the diagnostic says my engine needs repair? +
blocks.answer: If the diagnostic confirms an isolated failure, get repair quotes. Timing chain £650-£1,800, head gasket £800-£2,000, turbo £700-£2,500, injectors £400-£1,200.

blocks.question: Do I need to tell the DVLA and my insurer about diagnostics? +
blocks.answer: No - diagnostics are testing only. If repairs or replacement are performed, you may need to notify the DVLA and your insurer.
